goal: i wanna make a double inverted pendulum using a rack and pinion motor on cart motion system. Items: 12V DC motor, M1 8mm 26T gear, HGR20 400mm linear rail + HGH20CA block, 10mm ID flanged bearings, 2x VL53L0X TOF sensor, M1 10x10 400mm rack, 2x AS5600 magnetic encoder, Teensy 4.1, DRV8874 H-bridge motor driver, 12V 2A power supply, 12V to 3V3 regulator.

plan.title: Double inverted pendulum
plan.summary: A cart on a linear rail balances two hinged arms upright. A 12 V gearmotor drives the cart through a rack and pinion, two AS5600 encoders read the joint angles, two VL53L0X sensors track the cart, and a Teensy 4.1 runs the loop.
plan.final_result: The finished double inverted pendulum, every part in place and every wire connected.
safety: Keep the power supply unplugged until the last wire is in.
Keep fingers clear of moving parts (gears, belts, rails) when it runs.

part_guide.base-plate: Base plate 500 x 115 mm · 500 × 115 × 10 mm. 10 mm plywood or aluminium plate. Its front edge goes at the edge of the table (or on legs) so the pendulum can hang down.
part_guide.rail: HGR20 linear rail, 400 mm · 400 × 20 × 17.5 mm. HIWIN-style HGR20 profile: 20 mm wide, 17.5 mm tall. M5 screws every 60 mm into the base plate.
part_guide.block: HGH20CA carriage block · 61.4 × 44 × 25.4 mm. Rides on the HGR20 rail; the 20 mm channel wraps the rail. 30 mm from the rail's bottom to the block's top. 4x M5 on top for the cart plate.
part_guide.riser: Rack riser, 400 mm · 400 × 10 × 19 mm. Printed or aluminium spacer that lifts the rack so the pinion meshes just under the cart plate.
part_guide.rack: Gear rack M1 10 x 10, 400 mm · 400 × 10 × 10 mm. Module 1 rack, 10 x 10 mm section, 127 teeth. The teeth face the rail (-y); pitch line 1 mm in from the tooth tips.
part_guide.cart: Cart plate 120 x 90 mm · 120 × 90 × 6 mm. Bolts onto the carriage block. The motor shaft drops through the 9 mm hole to the pinion underneath.
part_guide.pinion: Pinion gear M1 26T (8 mm bore) · 28 × 28 × 10 mm. Module 1, 26 teeth: 26 mm pitch diameter, 28 mm outside, 10 mm face. 81.7 mm of cart travel per motor turn.
part_guide.motor: 12 V DC gearmotor (37 mm) · 37 × 37 × 72 mm. 37 mm gearmotor: 55 mm body, 6 mm output shaft 17 mm long, pointing down (-z). If the pinion's bore is 8 mm, use a 6-to-8 mm sleeve or a 6 mm-bore pinion.
part_guide.pivot: Pivot block · 30 × 20 × 30 mm. Holds the cart joint's two bearings (19 mm bore through). Screws to the cart plate.
part_guide.bearing-front: Flanged bearing 10 mm ID (F6800ZZ) · 21 × 21 × 6 mm. 10 mm bore, 19 mm outside, 5 mm wide, 21 mm flange 1 mm thick. Presses into a 19 mm pocket with the flange on the outside.
part_guide.bearing-back: Flanged bearing 10 mm ID (F6800ZZ) · 21 × 21 × 6 mm. 10 mm bore, 19 mm outside, 5 mm wide, 21 mm flange 1 mm thick. Presses into a 19 mm pocket with the flange on the outside.
part_guide.shaft-cart: Steel shaft 10 mm x 48 mm · 10 × 10 × 48 mm. Cut from 10 mm rod (h7, modelled 9.9 mm so it slides in the bearings). Cart joint: through both pivot-block bearings into the lower arm.
part_guide.arm-lower: Lower pendulum arm · 30 × 8 × 210 mm. Clamped to the cart shaft at the bottom (10 mm hole); a flanged bearing in the 19 mm hole at the top.
part_guide.magnet-cart: Diametric magnet 6 x 2.5 mm · 6 × 6 × 2.5 mm. Comes with the AS5600 board. Glue it centred on the shaft end.
part_guide.mount-cart: Encoder mount · 30 × 6.5 × 30 mm. Holds an AS5600 board 1 mm from the magnet on the shaft end (12 mm hole for the magnet).
part_guide.enc-cart: AS5600 magnetic encoder board · 23 × 23 × 1.6 mm. 12-bit angle sensor, I2C address 0x36 (fixed), so each one needs its own I2C bus. Chip side faces the magnet, 0.5 to 3 mm away.
part_guide.bearing-elbow: Flanged bearing 10 mm ID (F6800ZZ) · 21 × 21 × 6 mm. 10 mm bore, 19 mm outside, 5 mm wide, 21 mm flange 1 mm thick. Presses into a 19 mm pocket with the flange on the outside.
part_guide.shaft-elbow: Steel shaft 10 mm x 26 mm · 10 × 10 × 26 mm. Cut from 10 mm rod. Elbow joint: through the lower arm's bearing into the upper arm.
part_guide.arm-upper: Upper pendulum arm · 30 × 8 × 210 mm. Clamped to the elbow shaft at the bottom (10 mm hole). Free at the top.
part_guide.magnet-elbow: Diametric magnet 6 x 2.5 mm · 6 × 6 × 2.5 mm. Comes with the AS5600 board. Glue it centred on the shaft end.
part_guide.mount-elbow: Encoder mount · 30 × 6.5 × 30 mm. Holds an AS5600 board 1 mm from the magnet on the shaft end (12 mm hole for the magnet).
part_guide.enc-elbow: AS5600 magnetic encoder board · 23 × 23 × 1.6 mm. 12-bit angle sensor, I2C address 0x36 (fixed), so each one needs its own I2C bus. Chip side faces the magnet, 0.5 to 3 mm away.
part_guide.tof-bracket-left: Distance sensor bracket · 10 × 30 × 35 mm. Holds a VL53L0X board at the end of the rail, facing the carriage.
part_guide.tof-left: VL53L0X distance sensor board · 10.7 × 25 × 2.5 mm. Time-of-flight distance sensor, up to about 1.2 m, I2C address 0x29. Faces the carriage to measure where the cart is.
part_guide.tof-bracket-right: Distance sensor bracket · 10 × 30 × 35 mm. Holds a VL53L0X board at the end of the rail, facing the carriage.
part_guide.tof-right: VL53L0X distance sensor board · 10.7 × 25 × 2.5 mm. Time-of-flight distance sensor, up to about 1.2 m, I2C address 0x29. Faces the carriage to measure where the cart is.
part_guide.teensy: Teensy 4.1 · 60.96 × 17.78 × 1.6 mm. 600 MHz Cortex-M7, 3 I2C buses (Wire 18/19, Wire1 17/16). Powered over USB here; its pins are 3.3 V only.
part_guide.driver: DRV8874 motor driver board · 15.24 × 17.78 × 1.6 mm. H-bridge, motor supply 4.5 to 37 V on VIN, 2.1 A continuous. PMODE high = IN/IN (PWM) mode; SLEEP high to run. VM is the reverse-protected motor voltage, an output.
part_guide.regulator: 12 V to 3.3 V regulator · 22 × 17 × 5 mm. Small step-down module. Powers the four sensors from the 12 V supply.
part_guide.psu: 12 V 2 A power adapter · 85 × 50 × 32 mm. Wall adapter. Feeds the motor driver (VIN) and the 3.3 V regulator.

plan.title: Double inverted pendulum
plan.summary: A cart on a linear rail balances two hinged arms upright. A 12 V gearmotor drives the cart through a rack and pinion, two AS5600 encoders read the joint angles, two VL53L0X sensors track the cart, and a Teensy 4.1 runs the loop.

steps.title: Lay out the base plate
steps.instruction: Put the base plate on the table with its long front edge right at the table edge.
steps.check: The base plate lies flat with its front edge at the edge of the table.

placements.what: Base plate
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Screw down the linear rail
steps.instruction: Lay the rail along the base, 35 mm in from the back of the front strip, and screw it down with M5 screws.
steps.check: The rail runs straight along the base, 50 mm from each end.

placements.what: Linear rail
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Slide on the carriage block
steps.instruction: Slide the carriage block onto the rail from one end. Keep it level so the balls stay in.
steps.check: The block sits on the rail and slides end to end smoothly.

placements.what: Carriage block
placements.where: Slide on from the end, don't lift it off again

steps.title: Fit the rack riser
steps.instruction: Screw the rack riser along the back of the base, parallel to the rail.
steps.check: The riser runs along the back edge, parallel to the rail.

placements.what: Rack riser
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Fit the gear rack
steps.instruction: Screw the rack on top of the riser with its teeth facing the rail.
steps.check: The rack sits on the riser with its teeth facing the rail.

placements.what: Gear rack
placements.where: Teeth face the rail

steps.title: Bolt on the cart plate
steps.instruction: Put the cart plate on the carriage block, motor hole at the back over the rack, and bolt it down with 4 M5 screws.
steps.check: The cart plate sits flat on the block with its hole above the rack.

placements.what: Cart plate
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Mount the drive motor
steps.instruction: Stand the motor on the cart plate and push its shaft down through the hole. Screw it to the plate.
steps.check: The motor stands upright on the cart with its shaft through the plate.

placements.what: Drive motor
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Fit the pinion gear
steps.instruction: From underneath, push the pinion onto the motor shaft so it meshes with the rack, then tighten its set screw.
steps.check: The pinion is on the motor shaft under the cart and its teeth sit in the rack.

placements.what: Pinion gear
placements.where: Teeth mesh with the rack, no gap

steps.title: Screw on the pivot block
steps.instruction: Screw the pivot block to the front of the cart plate, its big hole running front to back.
steps.check: The pivot block sits at the front of the cart with its hole running front to back.

placements.what: Pivot block
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Press in the front cart bearing
steps.instruction: Press a flanged bearing into the front of the pivot block, flange outside.
steps.check: A bearing flange sits flat on the front face of the pivot block.

placements.what: Front cart bearing
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Press in the back cart bearing
steps.instruction: Press the second bearing into the back of the pivot block, flange outside.
steps.check: A bearing flange sits flat on the back face of the pivot block.

placements.what: Back cart bearing
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Fit the lower arm
steps.instruction: Hold the lower arm in front of the pivot block, its small hole lined up with the bearings.
steps.check: The lower arm stands in front of the cart, small hole at the bottom by the bearings.

placements.what: Lower arm
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Slide in the cart shaft
steps.instruction: Push the 48 mm shaft from the front through the arm and both bearings, then clamp the arm to it.
steps.check: The shaft passes through the arm and both bearings and pokes out of the back of the pivot block.

placements.what: Cart shaft
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Glue on the cart magnet
steps.instruction: Glue the round magnet centred on the back end of the cart shaft.
steps.check: A small round magnet sits in the middle of the shaft's back end.

placements.what: Cart joint magnet
placements.where: Centred on the shaft end

steps.title: Fit the cart encoder mount
steps.instruction: Screw the encoder mount to the cart behind the pivot block, its hole around the magnet.
steps.check: The mount stands behind the pivot block and the magnet is inside its hole.

placements.what: Cart encoder mount
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Screw on the cart encoder
steps.instruction: Screw an AS5600 board to the back of the mount, chip facing the magnet.
steps.check: The encoder board covers the mount's hole, pins at the bottom.

placements.what: Cart joint encoder
placements.where: Chip side faces the magnet

steps.title: Press in the elbow bearing
steps.instruction: Press a bearing into the big hole at the top of the lower arm, flange at the front.
steps.check: A bearing flange sits on the front of the lower arm's top hole.

placements.what: Elbow bearing
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Fit the upper arm
steps.instruction: Hold the upper arm in front of the lower arm, its hole lined up with the elbow bearing.
steps.check: The upper arm overlaps the top of the lower arm, in front of it.

placements.what: Upper arm
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Slide in the elbow shaft
steps.instruction: Push the 26 mm shaft from the front through the upper arm and the elbow bearing, then clamp the upper arm to it.
steps.check: The elbow shaft joins the two arms and the upper arm swings freely.

placements.what: Elbow shaft
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Glue on the elbow magnet
steps.instruction: Glue the second magnet centred on the back end of the elbow shaft.
steps.check: A small round magnet sits in the middle of the elbow shaft's back end.

placements.what: Elbow magnet
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Fit the elbow encoder mount
steps.instruction: Screw the second encoder mount to the back of the lower arm, its hole around the magnet.
steps.check: The mount sits on the back of the lower arm's top end.

placements.what: Elbow encoder mount
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Screw on the elbow encoder
steps.instruction: Screw the second AS5600 board to the mount, chip facing the magnet.
steps.check: The second encoder board covers the elbow mount's hole.

placements.what: Elbow encoder
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Fit the left distance sensor
steps.instruction: Screw a bracket to the left end of the base and a VL53L0X to it, sensor facing the cart.
steps.check: A distance sensor stands at the left end of the rail, facing the cart.

placements.what: Left sensor bracket
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

placements.what: Left distance sensor
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Fit the right distance sensor

steps.check: A distance sensor stands at the right end of the rail, facing the cart.

placements.what: Right distance sensor
placements.where: the highlighted part in the 3D model

steps.title: Place the Teensy
steps.instruction: Stick the Teensy to the front strip of the base, USB port to the left.
